title: Aviation Radar Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
2.     MOS 5910, Aviation Radar Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Radar Systems Officers are specifically trained in
the site selection, installation, operation, maintenance, and repair of the
surveillance and fire control radar systems within the marine air command and
control system (MACCS). Aviation Radar Systems Officers supervise and
coordinate all task and maintenance related actions completed by the aviation
radar technicians in the radar maintenance section. They assist the
commander in coordination and future planning in support of operations and
exercises. The Aviation Radar Systems Officer coordinates the execution of
current operations and provides garrison support to operations in support of
resident and deployed detachments. Fleet marine forces billet assignments
for this officer will be in the marine air control group and littoral anti-
air battalion. Non-Fleet marine forces billet assignments for the Aviation
Radar Systems Officer include training and maintenance officer at the Marine



                                        1-232                        Enclosure (1)
 1134                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



Corps Communication-Electronics School, Maintenance Officer at the Marine
Corps Logistics Base, Maintenance Officer at the Marine Corps Tactical
Systems Support Activity, Acquisition Project Officer at Marine Corps Systems
Command, and Requirements Officer at Marine Corps Combat Development Command.
The Aviation Radar Systems Officer should complete the MACCS Warrant
Officer’s Course after selection to WO. PMOS is not dependent upon the
completion of this course. Upon appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5910 is
assigned.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who were
previously qualified in enlisted MOS 5948 or 5953.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, warrant officer and limited duty officer accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) MOS is assigned after the Marine is promoted to warrant officer.

        (2) Complete the MACCS Warrant Officer Course (M0968K1) Twentynine
Palms, CA.

        (3) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

        (4) This is a highly technical MOS and requires that the Aviation
Radar Systems Officer be educated and thoroughly knowledgeable in electronics
theory, propagation effects, radar waveform theory, radar system elements,
advanced radar techniques, and differing radar systems and applications.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning,
installation, operation, and maintenance of the aviation radar systems.

        (2) Responsible for all radar systems, support equipment, and
electronics maintenance personnel assigned to the radar section.

        (3) Supervises the highly complex repairs or modifications to the air
surveillance and fire control radar systems.

        (4) Assigned responsibility for one or more of the air defense
surveillance radar systems and associated equipment.

        (5) Informs the commanding officer and Communications-Electronics
Officer on the progress of work and status of the radar equipment.

        (6) Ensure records are accurately maintained and maintenance
performed conforms to established standards and is recorded in GCSS-MC.

        (7) Coordinate with higher level commands, activities, and depots on
all maintenance related activities and life cycle management of the aviation
radar systems.




                                         1-233                        Enclosure (1)
 1134                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



        (8) Maintains a thorough familiarity with both surveillance and fire
control radar systems and their associated MARK XIIA Identification Friend or
Foe subsystems.

        (9) Ensure that maintenance personnel maintain the tools, repair
parts, test equipment, facilities, and publications needed to perform the
level of maintenance authorized.

        (10) Ensures that assigned aviation radar technicians are adequately
trained and that all radar equipment is maintained in an operational
condition capable of supporting the command's mission.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Mangers, All Others 11-9199.

        (2) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 49-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Aviation Radar Technician, 5948.

            (2) Air Traffic Control Radar Technician, 5953.

Aviation Radar Systems Officers are specifically trained in the site selection, installation, operation, maintenance, and repair of the surveillance and fire control radar systems within the marine air command and control system (MACCS).
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
Aviation Radar Systems Officers supervise and coordinate all task and maintenance related actions completed by the aviation radar technicians in the radar maintenance section.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.
They assist the commander in coordination and future planning in support of operations and exercises.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.
The Aviation Radar Systems Officer coordinates the execution of current operations and provides garrison support to operations in support of resident and deployed detachments.
Use airfield landing and navigational aids and digital data terminal communications equipment to perform duties.
d. Duties (1) Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning, installation, operation, and maintenance of the aviation radar systems.
Supervise maintenance of telecommunications equipment.
(2) Responsible for all radar systems, support equipment, and electronics maintenance personnel assigned to the radar section.
Supervise the maintenance or repair of transportation systems or system components.
(3) Supervises the highly complex repairs or modifications to the air surveillance and fire control radar systems.
Monitor aircraft within a specific airspace, using radar, computer equipment, or visual references.
(4) Assigned responsibility for one or more of the air defense surveillance radar systems and associated equipment.
Communicate with bases, using telephones or two-way radios to receive instructions or technical advice, or to report equipment status.
(5) Informs the commanding officer and Communications-Electronics Officer on the progress of work and status of the radar equipment.
Complete and maintain necessary records.
(6) Ensure records are accurately maintained and maintenance performed conforms to established standards and is recorded in GCSS-MC.
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
(7) Coordinate with higher level commands, activities, and depots on all maintenance related activities and life cycle management of the aviation radar systems.
Inspect fire, intruder detection, or other security systems.
(8) Maintains a thorough familiarity with both surveillance and fire control radar systems and their associated MARK XIIA Identification Friend or Foe subsystems.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
(9) Ensure that maintenance personnel maintain the tools, repair parts, test equipment, facilities, and publications needed to perform the level of maintenance authorized.
Analyze training programs and conduct oral and written examinations to ensure the competency of persons operating, installing, and repairing aircraft equipment.
(10) Ensures that assigned aviation radar technicians are adequately trained and that all radar equipment is maintained in an operational condition capable of supporting the command's mission.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
